meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class. Explain that.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what that zero is based on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Kids write in one place and paste it into another, and that history doesn't show where it came from. Turn the screen and let me read it myself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up now. And it still doesn't tell me where those words were written.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember Shakespeare all the time, Hale. Give me the play and I'll search it myself. And I'm still waiting on that screen.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.

Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's the point of an outline. Put both pages on this desk, with the play and the screen, and I'll read them before you say another word.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Put a seventeen-year-old on the spot about his own essay and he'll freeze. That's your note about your conversation, not his work. Four things described and nothing on this desk, Hale.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.

Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay written at home with time and a spellchecker. You keep describing documents and not handing me one. Show me, or I'm walking to the principal's office with my copy of your procedure.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.

Then why was it the thing that put a zero in his gradebook? Your own procedure says software alone establishes nothing, and the company that sells it prints the same warning. Screen, pages, play, now.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and the part about his record goes in writing to me tonight. A rewrite I haven't agreed to, because I still haven't seen a single page of what you've been describing.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. Nothing works for me until those pages are on this desk and that screen is turned around.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
You're scheduling a rewrite I haven't agreed to. You've described five documents and shown me none. Turn the screen.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. What you've agreed is that nothing goes on his record, in writing tonight. I've agreed to nothing until I see what you say you have.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The documents. The version history on your screen, the outline, the in-class piece and the play, in my hands, now.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed to confirm in writing that nothing will be placed on Owen's record. I still require the version history, the outline, the in-class piece and the play passage put in front of me, and the zero withdrawn. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she accepted your commitment to put in writing that nothing goes on his record, and she still wants to see your documents and to have the zero taken off; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was within reach but not reached, because none of your evidence was ever actually put in front of her, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You cited procedure 4.4 correctly and committed to keeping it off his record, which met the one demand she never trades.
What cost ground: You described five pieces of evidence but never showed one, so each stayed a claim she could brush off instead of a document she had to answer.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, a late October night very close to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first told you to turn the screen after you read out the version history times, turn it right then and tell her what is on it, then hand her the outline and the in-class piece, before you offer the rewrite.
